summary: Lift the shared durable-consumer skeleton — inventory and access implement the same protocol twice
description:
### Finding (architecture review R13, 2026-07-25)

`services/inventory/internal/consumer` and `services/access/internal/consumer` independently implement the same durable-consumer protocol:

- the consume loop and its termination handling (`waitConsume` and its equivalent),
- the readiness latch, including the serialization inventory added in TKT-90 to close the quarantine/latch race,
- quarantine-on-unknown-schema,
- backoff and `MaxDeliver` policy,
- envelope dedup on the deterministic id.

Same protocol, different code, different bugs — and the open backlog already shows it: TKT-121 (inventory's shutdown reports a clean exit as a consumer error), TKT-122 (access drains only already-arrived consumer errors) and TKT-123 (waitConsume's diagnostic can't distinguish causes) are three tickets against two copies of one loop.

### The constraint that matters

This is a refactor **behind existing tests**. The guarantees proven by TKT-90, TKT-97 and TKT-99 — and ADR-017's rule that termination is loudly unready and never self-heals — must survive. A test that has to be rewritten to pass is not a chore; it means a guarantee moved, and it gets investigated before anything is edited.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The consume loop, termination handling and readiness latch exist once and are consumed by both services.
- [ ] Each service keeps only its per-subject handlers and its own quarantine store behind an interface.
- [ ] TKT-90, TKT-97 and TKT-99's tests pass **unmodified**.
- [ ] The `schema <= 0` bottom-end rule and the must-not-touch-readiness clause survive verbatim.
- [ ] `make check` green.

**Blocked by TKT-126** — the skeleton decodes envelopes, so the shared envelope lands first.

objective.note: inventory and access each implement the same durable-consumer protocol — readiness latching, quarantine on unknown schema, backoff policy, envelope dedup, consume-context termination — as independent code with independent bugs. Lift the skeleton so one fix reaches both.

scope.note: IN: lifting the consume loop, waitConsume/termination handling, the readiness latch and its serialization, backoff/MaxDeliver policy parsing, and envelope dedup into shared/go/events; leaving the per-subject handlers and the per-service quarantine store behind an interface. OUT: the envelope type itself (TKT-126); changing any readiness or termination GUARANTEE; the quarantine table schemas (they stay per-service).

uncertainties.note: How much of the quarantine contract generalizes. The two services quarantine into different tables with different columns, and inventory additionally latches readiness off pending quarantine while access does not. The shared piece may be an interface plus the latch, with the store contract staying per-service. Plan-time call; the COS holds either way.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-126 — the skeleton decodes envelopes, so the shared envelope type must exist first. Linked.

approach.note: This is a refactor behind existing tests, not a redesign. Every guarantee currently proven — TKT-90's readiness/skew reorder, TKT-97's reaction to ConsumeContext.Closed(), TKT-99's broker-level durable-deletion proof, ADR-017's loudly-unready-on-termination rule — must still be proven by its existing test, ideally unmodified. A test that needs rewriting to pass is a signal the guarantee moved, and must be treated as a finding, not a chore.

first_slice.note: Lift the smallest genuinely-identical piece first: waitConsume plus the readiness latch (already near-identical between the two services). Quarantine and backoff follow only if the first slice shows the interface holds. If the two quarantine paths turn out not to generalize, stopping after the first slice is an acceptable close — record why in the ticket.

success.note: COS: (1) the consume loop, termination handling and readiness latch exist once, consumed by both inventory and access; (2) each service retains only per-subject handlers and its own quarantine store; (3) TKT-90, TKT-97 and TKT-99's tests pass UNMODIFIED — any test that needs editing is investigated as a moved guarantee before it is edited; (4) the `schema <= 0` bottom-end rule and the must-not-touch-readiness clause survive verbatim; (5) make check green.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-017 (§ the loudly-unready-on-durable-deletion guarantee, the poison/skew line and its bottom end, the readiness clause), ADR-009 (acked publishes, deterministic ids, dedup), ADR-022 (out-of-band migrations — the quarantine tables stay per-service and keep their own migration ownership). Prior work whose guarantees must survive: TKT-90 (readiness/skew reorder race), TKT-97 (waitConsume reaction), TKT-99 (broker-level durable-deletion proof).

binding.rule: Domain event schema evolution: bump on consumer semantics, not parse compatibility. A consumer must dispatch on `schema` before decoding `data`. The poison/skew line has a bottom end (`schema <= 0` is a broken envelope, not the future). A fixture built from the type under test cannot fail.

APIs are contract-first: the OpenAPI spec is the source of truth, served by the service at /openapi.yaml and checked for drift in the gate; domain events use a versioned platform envelope (id, type==subject, occurred_at, schema, data) published to JetStream with acks (never fire-and-forget), with a deterministic envelope id so retried/raced emissions de-duplicate.
Migrations run out-of-band: each binary's `migrate` subcommand, as a one-shot Compose job the service waits on. The server path never migrates.

reference.summary: The termination guarantee whose test must survive unmodified

Codex session `019fa6d8-c2a3-7231-9e40-7c2f99470279`. Brief included the ticket, the COS, the deferred DoR item, the shaped first slice, the four governing ADRs **re-resolved at claim time**, my own verified survey of what is actually duplicated at HEAD, and the exact traps in each pinned test.

Critique by `main-agent` follows in `kind=plan-final`. The draft is reproduced verbatim below.

# TKT-127 execution plan

## 1. Decision

Create `ticketing/shared/durableconsumer` containing the genuinely common behavior: a zero-value readiness state with serialized decisions, plus the blocking wait/termination select currently implemented by access’s `waitConsume`. Keep access’s package-local `waitConsume` symbol as a thin, signature-compatible delegate so the four TKT-97 tests remain unchanged and continue exercising the production path. Inventory will adopt that same delegate and begin observing `ConsumeContext.Closed()`; this is an intentional behavior addition, not a pure refactor, and receives its own RED test.

The deferred quarantine question resolves to **no shared quarantine contract**: inventory quarantines and acknowledges, while access parks with delayed NAKs and has no quarantine store. Stop after the shaped first slice and record why; backoff, `MaxDeliver`, envelope validation, disposition, and store-level dedup remain outside this ticket.

## 2. Does this earn a `shared/go` entry?

Yes, narrowly. The behavior is used by three durable consumers across two independently built service modules, and it carries the ADR-017 invariant that asynchronous termination becomes loudly unready and cannot self-heal. A service-local package cannot be shared across the Go module boundary, while copying it into inventory would preserve the drift that produced the finding.

Create **ADR-034: Shared durable-consumer lifecycle primitive**. Its Decision section should say:

> We add `ticketing/shared/durableconsumer` as a narrow behavioral-kernel entry. It owns a zero-value `Readiness` state, the serialization primitive needed when readiness is derived concurrently, and `Wait`, which distinguishes parent cancellation from asynchronous consume-context termination, latches false only for the latter, and preserves the existing diagnostic exactly. It does not import JetStream or `domainevent`; create/update configuration, handler registration, startup gates, envelope validation, known schema ranges, disposition, retry schedules, quarantine persistence, and dedup remain service-owned.

This earns the kernel entry because it centralizes cross-service lifecycle behavior without becoming the consumer framework ADR-033 rejected.

## 3. Alternatives considered

### A. Shared wait plus serialized readiness, with service adapters — chosen

**Cons**

- Adds a shared-kernel concept for a relatively small amount of code.
- Inventory gains asynchronous durable-deletion detection, so the change is not behavior-neutral.
- `Readiness.Store` must remain available for existing tests and simple lifecycle sites; callers could bypass serialized decisions if used carelessly.

**Pros**

- Removes the actual common termination behavior while preserving all existing test seams.
- Moves `readinessMu` into a reusable zero-value type without changing `c.ready.Store(false)` or `c.Ready()`.
- Requires no NATS, database, or domain-event dependency in `shared/go`.
- Preserves every service-specific disposition and startup ordering.

The Cons do not negate the choice: ADR-034 governs the kernel addition, the inventory behavior gets a dedicated test, and both racing inventory decisions are explicitly required to use the serialized API.

### B. Full shared consumer framework

Lift JetStream creation, `Consume`, handler dispatch, schema checks, disposition, backoff, quarantine, and dedup.

**Cons**

- Contradicts ADR-033: inventory quarantines and acks; access parks outstanding.
- Backoff is not duplicated: access’s issuer has configurable backoff, policy and inventory use different hardcoded delays.
- Dedup is implemented transactionally in service stores, not in the consumer loop.
- Would move the TKT-97 guarantee away from its package-local production seam.
- Would add NATS and service-policy concepts to the shared kernel.

**Pros**

- Produces the largest apparent reduction in consumer-package code.
- Could provide a future standard starting point for new consumers.

Rejected because the common framework would encode a union of unrelated policies or flatten differences the services depend on.

### C. Copy access’s helper into inventory

**Cons**

- Fails COS 1: lifecycle behavior would still exist twice.
- Future fixes such as TKT-123 would still require coordinated edits.
- Leaves inventory’s readiness serialization as an independent implementation.

**Pros**

- No shared-kernel ADR or module-level abstraction.
- Smallest immediate diff.

Rejected because it preserves the architectural defect rather than resolving it.

## 4. DoD mapped 1:1 to the COS

- [ ] **COS 1 — one lifecycle core:** `durableconsumer.Wait` owns the blocking termination select and exact error construction; `durableconsumer.Readiness` owns atomic state and serialization. Both access consumers and inventory call the package-local delegate into this implementation.
- [ ] **COS 2 — service policy remains local:** inventory retains `catalogStore`, `QuarantineCatalogEvent`, pending-quarantine startup logic, and quarantine dispositions. Access retains parking behavior and has no invented quarantine interface. Durable configuration and startup gates also remain local because they are demonstrably different. Record in TKT-127 that the literal “only per-subject handlers” wording was scoped down under the shaped stopping rule.
- [ ] **COS 3 — tests remain untouched:** all TKT-90, TKT-97, and TKT-99 tests pass byte-for-byte unmodified. Any discovered need to edit one stops implementation as a moved-guarantee finding.
- [ ] **COS 4 — poison/skew invariant:** make no changes to either service’s envelope dispatch or bottom-end tests. Existing `schema <= 0` and “must not touch readiness” code, comments, and hand-written fixtures remain unchanged.
- [ ] **COS 5 — gate:** run focused Go tests, the shared-package race test, then `make check`.

## 5. Files

### Create

- `docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md` — ADR-033-style argument, alternatives, boundary, decision, and consequences.
- `shared/go/durableconsumer/run.go` — `Readiness`, its serialized-decision method, atomic-state adapter, and `Wait`.
- `shared/go/durableconsumer/run_test.go` — RED-first tests for termination, clean shutdown, exact diagnostic, and serialized readiness.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run.go` — package-local `waitConsume` delegate matching access’s compatibility seam.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go` — inventory’s deliberate asynchronous-termination behavior test.

### Modify

- `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go` — retain the existing unexported symbol and exact `*atomic.Bool` signature, but delegate its body to `durableconsumer.Wait`.
- `services/access/internal/consumer/consumer.go` — replace the local atomic readiness field with `durableconsumer.Readiness`; pass its atomic state to the existing `waitConsume` call. Leave handler and retry logic unchanged.
- `services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go` — use `durableconsumer.Readiness`; preserve backlog-drain ordering and the existing `waitConsume` call.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go` — use `durableconsumer.Readiness`, remove `readinessMu`, serialize the two TKT-90 readiness decisions, and call `waitConsume(ctx, cc.Closed(), …, "inventory-catalog-offering")` after `startupConverge`.
- TKT-127’s git-derived board record — record that quarantine/backoff/dedup did not generalize and the ticket intentionally stopped after the shaped first slice.

### Delete

None.

`shared/go/go.mod` and `shared/go/go.sum` should not change: the package needs only the standard library.

## 6. Test plan

### Primary seam: `shared/go/durableconsumer/run_test.go`

Write these tests first:

- `TestWaitAsyncTerminationLatchesUnreadyAndReturnsExactDiagnostic`
  - Starts ready, closes only the consume-context channel, and asserts readiness becomes false.
  - Asserts the exact error: `test-consumer: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)`.
  - **RED today:** the package and `Wait` do not exist.

- `TestWaitCleanShutdownLeavesReadinessUntouched`
  - Cancels only the parent context.
  - Asserts `nil` and that readiness remains true; the caller’s defer owns clean-shutdown latching.
  - **RED today:** the package and `Wait` do not exist.

- `TestReadinessSerializesStartupTrueAgainstCommittedSkewLatch`
  - Deterministically stages a startup decision inside the serialized section and a later skew latch waiting behind it.
  - Releases startup and asserts the skew decision runs last, leaving readiness false.
  - This pins the TKT-90 ordering: quarantine persistence happens before entering the latch section.
  - **RED today:** there is no shared readiness type or serialized decision API.

Run this package under `go test -race`.

### Inventory adoption seam: `services/inventory/internal/consumer/run_test.go`

- `TestWaitConsumeAsyncTerminationLatchesInventoryUnreadyAndNamesDurable`
  - Calls the new package-local delegate with a hand-closed channel.
  - Asserts readiness becomes false and the exact error names `inventory-catalog-offering`.
  - **RED today:** inventory has no `waitConsume` symbol and does not observe `cc.Closed()`.

No new test touches schema, wire format, or compatibility. All existing schema tests continue using their hand-written literal bytes; no fixture may be built from the Go type under test.

### Verification order

1. Run shared tests RED, then green.
2. Run access consumer tests unchanged.
3. Run inventory consumer tests, including the new RED-first adoption test.
4. Run `go test -race` for `shared/go/durableconsumer`.
5. Run `make check`, which includes the TKT-99 broker-level smoke proof.

## 7. Unmodified-tests proof

### TKT-97 — `services/access/internal/consumer/run_test.go`

- `TestWaitConsumeAsyncTerminationLatchesUnreadyAndErrors`
  - The package-local `waitConsume` symbol remains.
  - Its `*atomic.Bool` parameter remains accepted.
  - Production access call sites still go through this symbol, so the test does not become a decorative façade test.

- `TestWaitConsumeCleanShutdownStaysLatchedAndReturnsNil`
  - The shared `Wait` context arm returns `nil` without writing readiness.
  - Existing `Run` defers continue to latch false during unwind.

- `TestWaitConsumeTerminationErrorNamesConsumer`
  - The same name is passed into the one shared format string.
  - No wrapping is added in `waitConsume`.

- `TestWaitConsumeTerminationWinsOverLiveContext`
  - The shared implementation retains the same two-arm select.
  - With a live context and closed consume channel, only termination is eligible.

No line in `run_test.go` changes.

### TKT-99 smoke literal

The literal remains:

```text
access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)
```

It remains byte-identical because:

1. `durableconsumer.Wait` uses the existing format string unchanged.
2. Access’s package-local `waitConsume` returns that error unchanged.
3. `PolicyConsumer.Run` still passes `access-slot-policy` and returns the error unwrapped.
4. `cmd/access/main.go` is untouched and retains the `access: ` prefix.

`smoke/access_consumer_test.go` is not edited.

### TKT-90 field accesses and readiness assertions

`Consumer` keeps an unexported field named `ready`. `durableconsumer.Readiness` exposes the same `Store(bool)` and `Load() bool` methods, so `c.ready.Store(false)` and every `c.Ready()` call compile unchanged and observe the same state.

The serialization moves behind that field:

- `refreshStartupReadiness` performs its pending-quarantine query and possible `true` store inside the serialized decision.
- The skew path calls `QuarantineCatalogEvent` first and enters the serialized decision only after that call returns.
- Preserve this sentence verbatim beside the inventory code: “Serialized, either order converges on unready — but only because the quarantine insert COMMITS before the latch is taken; latch first and the commit escapes the critical section, reopening the race.”

Neither `consumer_test.go` nor `reconcile_test.go` is edited.

## 8. TKT-121 / TKT-122 / TKT-123 / TKT-133

- **TKT-121 — still independent.** Inventory gains asynchronous consume-context termination, but its clean-shutdown `Run` tail still returns a `context.Canceled`-wrapped error that races `main`’s `<-ctx.Done()` branch. That is service-level shutdown arbitration, not the shared consume wait.
- **TKT-122 — still independent.** Waiting for one terminal result from each access consumer during bounded teardown belongs to `cmd/access.awaitShutdown`; a shared readiness/wait primitive cannot observe errors sent after the current snapshot drain.
- **TKT-123 — reshaped, not absorbed.** The ambiguous diagnostic is now produced once in `durableconsumer.Wait`, so the future fix has one owner. This ticket deliberately preserves the coarse wording because TKT-99 requires it verbatim; TKT-123 must add cause capture and update its smoke contract explicitly.
- **TKT-133 — still independent.** `type == subject` validation is a service-owned contract judgment with service-specific disposition and logging. Taking it here would mix envelope validation into the lifecycle primitive and expand a refactor already carrying inventory’s termination behavior change.

## 9. Risks

- **TKT-97 becomes disconnected from production.** Mitigation: both access production call sites continue calling the package-local `waitConsume` delegate; do not call `durableconsumer.Wait` directly from them.
- **The TKT-90 race is reopened during mutex removal.** Mitigation: both racing inventory decisions use the shared serialized API, while quarantine persistence remains outside and before the false-latch section; add the deterministic concurrency test.
- **Inventory begins exiting on durable deletion unexpectedly.** Mitigation: treat this as an explicit behavior addition, name the durable in the diagnostic, and add the inventory RED-first test. TKT-99 already proves the NATS `Closed()` mechanism against a real broker.
- **The shared package grows into a disposition framework.** Mitigation: ADR-034 forbids JetStream configuration, envelope decoding, schema ranges, ACK/NAK/Term choices, retry schedules, quarantine, and dedup.
- **Direct `Readiness.Store` bypasses serialization.** Mitigation: retain it only for compatibility and non-racing lifecycle writes; document and test that inventory’s two readiness-derived decisions must use the serialized method.

## 10. Migrations / auth / money / CI-config touch

- **Migrations:** no.
- **Authentication/authorization:** no.
- **Money paths:** no.
- **CI configuration:** no.
- **Generated code:** no.
- **Dependency files:** no expected change.

No files were modified while producing this plan.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### ✅ Plan final — TKT-127 (delta on the `kind=plan` draft)

Critique by **`main-agent`** (Claude Code, Opus 5) per `config.models.planReview` — cross-model against the `gpt-5.6-sol` draft. **The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Amendments only; unamended sections stand as drafted.

**Gate 2 was waived by the owner for this run** (see `kind=claim`). Every decision below that a human would normally have made is marked **[self-decided]** with its rationale, per the waiver's terms.

---

#### Seam verification — every file, symbol and claim the draft names, checked at HEAD

| Draft claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| access `waitConsume` in `run.go:32`, 2 call sites (`consumer.go:436`, `policy.go:218`) | ✅ confirmed |
| inventory has no `waitConsume`, `Run` blocks on `<-ctx.Done()` (`consumer.go:506`) | ✅ confirmed |
| inventory `Run` has `cc` in scope for `cc.Closed()` (`consumer.go:490`) | ✅ confirmed |
| `readinessMu` has exactly 2 users, both inventory, both in-package (`consumer.go:245`, `:462`) | ✅ confirmed |
| TKT-97 tests call unexported `waitConsume` with `&ready` (`*atomic.Bool`) | ✅ confirmed, 4 tests |
| TKT-99 smoke literal built from `run.go`'s format string + `policy.go`'s name + `main.go`'s prefix | ✅ confirmed verbatim |
| `c.ready.Store(false)` is a direct field access in `consumer_test.go:530` | ✅ confirmed |
| No `ADR-034` exists; next number is free | ✅ confirmed (max is ADR-033) |
| `shared/go/go.mod` needs no change | ✅ confirmed — **and neither does any service `go.mod`**: the repo uses a **`go.work` workspace** listing all 8 modules, which is how `ticketing/shared/domainevent` already resolves. The draft understated this; see **A6**. |
| Migrations / auth / money / CI-config / codegen untouched | ✅ confirmed — no stop-condition triggered |

Wire-level facts spot-checked, not just symbols: the format verb is `"%s: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)"` and `*atomic.Bool`'s method set is `Store(bool)` / `Load() bool` / `Swap` / `CompareAndSwap`.

---

#### A1 — **REJECT** `durableconsumer.Readiness`. Keep `ready atomic.Bool` and `readinessMu` exactly where they are. **[self-decided]**

This is the one substantive rejection, and it comes from reading the draft's own Cons against its own Decision before checking any code (`quality-practices.md` §1 — the cheapest possible reject).

The draft's Decision claims the shared package owns *"the serialization primitive needed when readiness is derived concurrently."* Its own **Con** says *"callers could bypass serialized decisions if used carelessly"*, and its own **Risk 5** is *"Direct `Readiness.Store` bypasses serialization — mitigation: document and test."*

Those two lines refute the Decision they appear in. Today `readinessMu` is an **unexported field in the same package as its only two writers**. It cannot be bypassed — not by convention, by construction. Replacing it with an exported kernel type whose `Store` skips the mutex converts a **structural** guarantee into a **documented** one, and "document and test" is not a mitigation for a guarantee that is currently unbypassable.

That matters more here than it normally would: **TKT-90 is one of the three guarantees COS 3 names as must-survive.** A refactor that weakens the enforcement of a guarantee it was told to preserve fails the ticket's central constraint, even while every one of its tests still passes. This is the TKT-62 shape — every fact in the draft correct, the synthesis wrong.

Two further reasons:
- **YAGNI at the kernel bar.** `readinessMu` serves 2 call sites in 1 service. Access has no check-then-latch race to serialize because it has no quarantine store. Lifting a mutex-plus-bool to serve one caller is speculative generality, and `shared/go` is explicitly the place where that bar is highest (ADR-033: *"a kernel that accumulates domain concepts stops being a kernel"*).
- **The readiness latch already exists once — it is `sync/atomic.Bool`.** Three structs each holding an `atomic.Bool` field is not duplicated *code*; it is three instances of one stdlib type. There is no lift available that the standard library has not already performed.

**Consequence:** the draft's `TestReadinessSerializesStartupTrueAgainstCommittedSkewLatch` is **dropped** (nothing to test), and its Risks 2 and 5 **disappear** rather than being mitigated. Inventory's `readinessMu` block and its load-bearing comment are not touched at all — which is a stronger answer to COS 3/COS 4 than preserving them through a migration.

#### A2 — **AMEND** the shared surface down to one function, with the signature unchanged **[self-decided]**

```go
// shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go
func Wait(ctx context.Context, closed <-chan struct{}, ready *atomic.Bool, name string) error
```

Body and doc comment moved **verbatim** from `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go`. `*atomic.Bool` rather than an interface: it is exactly what both existing call sites already hold (`&c.ready`), it keeps the TKT-97 signature byte-identical, and an interface would be a new concept bought for nothing. The package imports only `context`, `fmt`, `sync/atomic`.

`services/access/internal/consumer/run.go` keeps the unexported `waitConsume` with its exact signature and delegates in one line. **Why the delegate rather than editing the two call sites to call `durableconsumer.Wait` directly:** it is what keeps the four TKT-97 tests exercising the production path instead of becoming a façade — the draft got this right and it is the load-bearing reason the delegate exists, not a compatibility shim.

#### A3 — **ACCEPT** inventory adoption, and name it as a behaviour addition

Inventory gains `waitConsume` (its own one-line delegate, matching access's shape) and `Run` calls it after `startupConverge` with `"inventory-catalog-offering"`. Verified safe on the clean path: `Wait` returns `nil` on `ctx.Done()`, so `Run` falls through to the same `fmt.Errorf("consumer stopped: %w", ctx.Err())` it returns today — **clean shutdown is bit-for-bit unchanged**, and TKT-121's race is neither fixed nor worsened. On async termination inventory now latches unready and exits, which it does not do today. Gets its own RED-first test.

#### A4 — **ADD** a golden test pinning the exact diagnostic string

The TKT-99 smoke literal is currently protected only by a docker-based smoke run. Moving the format string to a new package is precisely when it can drift. Add to `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait_test.go` a test asserting the **hand-written literal**:

```
test-consumer: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)
```

Hand-written, **not** built from the format string — a fixture derived from the code under test cannot fail (ADR-017's trap, and `quality-practices.md` §1 states it as a rule). This is the only genuinely new guarantee this ticket adds, and it is worth its three lines: it moves the smoke suite's verbatim contract into a unit test that fails in seconds instead of after a container restart.

#### A5 — **ACCEPT** ADR-034, narrowed to match A1

`docs/adr/ADR-034-shared-durable-consumer-lifecycle.md`. Its Decision now covers one function, and its "line this package does not cross" section must additionally record **why readiness serialization stayed in inventory** (A1's argument) — that is the ADR's most useful content, because it is the boundary a future ticket will be tempted to cross.

#### A6 — **CORRECT** the module-wiring claim

The draft said `shared/go/go.mod` would not change. True, but incomplete: **no `go.mod` anywhere changes**, because `go.work` at the repo root already `use`s all 8 modules. Worth stating so the implementer does not "fix" a non-existent missing dependency and so a reviewer does not expect one.

#### A7 — **SCOPE DOWN** COS 1 and COS 2 explicitly, with reasons **[self-decided]**

The DoR's `first_slice` authorizes this: *"If the two quarantine paths turn out not to generalize, stopping after the first slice is an acceptable close — record why in the ticket."* They do not generalize; recording why:

- **COS 1 "the consume loop … exists once"** → delivered as *termination handling* exists once. The consume loop proper is `cons.Consume(func(msg){…})` — one line — and everything around it (stream lookup, inventory's orphan `DeleteConsumer`, the two different `consumerConfig`s, `startupConverge` vs. the backlog-drain gate) genuinely differs. The shared part of the loop **is** the termination wait.
- **COS 1 "readiness latch exists once"** → already true via `sync/atomic.Bool`; see A1.
- **COS 2 "each service keeps only its per-subject handlers and its own quarantine store behind an interface"** → each service keeps its handlers, its quarantine store, **and** its durable config and startup gate. Access gets **no** invented quarantine interface: it has no quarantine store to put behind one, and inventory's `catalogStore` interface already satisfies the "behind an interface" half.
- **Quarantine / backoff / `MaxDeliver` / dedup** → not lifted. The ticket's premise that these are duplicated is **false at HEAD**: access parks and inventory quarantines-and-acks (ADR-033 refused to flatten exactly this); options parsing exists in one consumer of three; dedup is store-owned SQL. Lifting any of them would invent a union of policies rather than remove a duplication.

*Assume this bounced at Gate 3. What went wrong?*
